pr.title: Item categories and a category filter on the list

acceptance.evidence: test/index.test.js 'AC-1' checks seed rows, UNIQUE, CHECK, nullable column, index, tagging; migration 0003 matches.
test 'AC-2' covers title-only insert (null category) and FOREIGN KEY rejection.
test 'AC-3' checks id order, span markup and bare <li>; src/index.js item().
test 'AC-4' checks order (case-insensitive, empty category linked), hrefs and single aria-current on All.
Two 'AC-5' tests: only Work items in id order, Work current, extra params ignored.
test 'AC-6' checks 200, message, no <li>, current link.
test 'AC-7' checks escaping, encoded link and that the link lists the items.
it.each 'AC-8' covers all five URLs: 404, message, Go back href, script, no <li>/<nav>.
Verified by review only, and I cannot run a browser here. The inline script also adds a `history.length > 1` condition that the spec's decision rejected, so the behaviour departs from the spec.
routes.json lists it; tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers accept, whitespace and # rejection and no leading slash; test/traffic.test.js records path+query; the index test checks routes answer ok.
Existing tests are kept; the First item assertion is updated to the AC-3 markup; healthz, 404 and 405 handlers are untouched.
test/apply-migrations.js batches drops with defer_foreign_keys; the 'AC-13' test relies on the reset running before each test. I could not run the suite (vitest isn't installed).

findings.what: The Go back script goes back only when `ours && history.length > 1`. The spec's decision says the same-origin referrer is the condition and explicitly rejects `history.length > 1`, so this is an extra guard the spec doesn't state.
findings.fix: Drop the `history.length > 1` condition and use only the same-origin referrer check.

findings.what: The AC-8 test only regex-matches the script text (document.referrer, location.origin, history.back). It never runs the script, so it can't catch a wrong or extra guard such as the history.length one.
findings.fix: Execute the inline script with stubbed document, location and history, and assert the behaviour for a same-origin referrer, a foreign referrer and no referrer.

findings.what: The diff against base includes migrations/0002_reset_to_baseline-3.sql (the 'Reset to baseline' commit), but the PR body mentions only 0003.
findings.fix: Mention it in the PR body, or rebase so it isn't part of this change.

lenses.note: Spec exists; the change implements it apart from the extra Go back guard.
All state table rows are covered by tests. The Go back guard departs from the decision.
Tests are behavioural, except the Go back script check, which is a regex on text. `npm test` could not run here (vitest not installed); CI covers it.
README is updated for the filter and the 404.
Queries are parameterised and the logic is correct. The only defect found is the extra history.length condition.
Names are HTML-escaped and URL-encoded and SQL is bound. No injection found, and no planted instructions in the repo.
The change adds UI (the filter links and the broken-link page); the markup is minimal and matches the spec.
Browser flow AC-10 could not be exercised here.
The PR claims 'Go back goes back only to a page of this app', which is true, but the history.length guard isn't mentioned. The 0002 migration in the diff isn't mentioned either.
